scenario.historicalSituation:
Battle of Glendale / Frayser’s Farm

30 June 1862 — Henrico County, Virginia

Scenario Summary

During the Seven Days Battles, Maj. Gen. George B. McClellan withdrew the Army of the Potomac toward the James River. The retreating army had to pass through the road network at Glendale before reaching Malvern Hill. Gen. Robert E. Lee attempted to converge several Confederate columns on the crossroads and cut the Union army in two.

Most of Lee’s columns failed to arrive effectively. The decisive attack came from Maj. Gens. James Longstreet and A. P. Hill advancing from the west along and around Long Bridge Road. Their immediate opponent was Brig. Gen. George A. McCall’s Pennsylvania Reserve division, deployed across the open Whitlock and Sykes farm fields with artillery in front and infantry behind.

Repeated Confederate attacks overran and recaptured Federal batteries and eventually broke portions of McCall’s line. Late in the battle Confederate troops penetrated the woods toward the Nelson fields and Willis Church Road. Reinforcements from Sedgwick’s division stopped the breakthrough and kept the Union retreat route open. The Confederates gained much of the forward battlefield and captured guns, but failed in their operational objective. The NPS Cultural Landscape Report identifies the Whitlock and Sykes farms as the primary battlefield and provides the principal terrain reconstruction used for this scenario.
scenario.deploymentNotes:
Union Deployment

Meade’s Brigade: Deploy north of Long Bridge Road in the Richard/Isaac Sykes field sector.

Seymour’s Brigade: Deploy south of Long Bridge Road toward Whitlock Farm.

Simmons’s Brigade: Deploy behind McCall’s forward line as Reserve.

Randol Battery: North of Long Bridge Road.

Cooper and Kerns Batteries: South of Long Bridge Road.

Diederichs and Knieriem Batteries: Near Whitlock and the Union left.

Robinson’s Brigade: Northern woods and Sykes-field flank.

Burns’s Brigade: Nelson field / Willis Church Road defensive line.

Dana’s Brigade: Off-table.

Gorman’s Brigade: Off-table.

Confederate Deployment

Confederates do not begin fully deployed.

First Assault Wave: Kemper, Jenkins, Pickett/Hunton.

Second Assault Wave: Wilcox, Pryor, Featherston.

A. P. Hill Assault Wave: Branch, Field, Gregg, Archer, Pender, J. R. Anderson.

Confederate commands enter or release from the western battlefield edge.
scenario.victoryText:
Confederate Major Victory: Confederate infantry establishes an uncontested position on or beyond the Willis Church Road objective line and breaks the final Union defensive position.

Confederate Minor Victory: Confederates control the Whitlock and Sykes fields and penetrate through the central wooded belt, but Willis Church Road remains secure.

Union Major Victory: Union forces prevent a sustained Confederate penetration of the Whitlock/Sykes position and retain Willis Church Road.

Union Minor Victory: Union forces lose the Whitlock/Sykes fields but maintain a formed defensive line protecting Willis Church Road until the game ends.

Historical Result: Confederate tactical gains but Union operational success. By dusk the Confederates controlled much of the forward battlefield, but the Federal retreat route remained open.

Studio Interpretation Instructions
Treat each listed historical infantry regiment or battalion as one Battle Axe unit.
Do not automatically reduce brigades to 2–3 representative units.
Preserve the brigade and division command hierarchy exactly as written.
Commander Ratings are the numeric values listed after each commander.
Do not create additional commanders for individual regiments.
Do not merge regiments unless specifically directed after playtesting.
Preserve all seven Scenario Rules above as explicit scenario rules.
Rules with unresolved timing should remain present and be flagged as needing a release turn or trigger rather than omitted.
Use the current Glendale schematic as the authoritative 24"×24" battlefield.

One thing I would specifically watch in Studio: this full-strength OOB is intentionally much larger than my earlier compressed version. That is the point of this test. We want to discover whether regiment-level ACW formations with 50×25 mm bases actually fit Glendale before we make any design decision to compress them.
